job.description: About Niantic Spatial   AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.  That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.  In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.  Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.     About the Role   You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. This is an end-to-end applied research role that spans from strong engineering and data-systems work to R&D in 3D deep learning, transformers, and foundation models. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems.  The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves.  You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable engineering — developing new approaches to geospatial registration, correspondence, and geometric optimization, then productionizing these technologies to directly improve Niantic Spatial's world model.     What You'll Do      Geospatial Registration  — Develop and advance algorithms for world-scale georeferencing and registration across imagery, 3D reconstructions, point clouds, and geographic reference data.     3D Geometry & Correspondence  — Build and improve methods spanning multi-view geometry, SfM, SLAM, feature matching, learned correspondence, bundle adjustment, point-cloud registration, and ICP.     Data & Evaluation  — Create the data and evaluation flywheel for world-scale mapping — design and maintain large-scale datasets, pipelines, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies that expose hard failure modes, accelerate research iteration, and support production.     Learning-Based 3D Reasoning  — Explore and develop learning-based approaches for geospatial understanding, combining transformers and 3D foundation models with geometric priors and uncertainty modeling.     Production Robustness  — Design robust solutions for challenging real-world conditions: sparse or noisy GPS, changing appearance, inconsistent reconstruction quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps.     Cross-Functional Collaboration  — Partner with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping — as well as engineering and product teams — to identify high-impact problems and turn research breakthroughs into end-to-end production systems.     Research Communication  — Share results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, and internal presentations; contribute to publications and open research where appropriate.       What You'll Bring     Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Photogrammetry, or a closely related field — or equivalent research or industry experience.    Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, machine learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related area.    Demonstrated experience with 3D geometry and several relevant areas — multi-view reconstruction, SfM, SLAM, camera pose estimation, point-cloud registration, image-based localization, georeferencing, or sensor fusion.    The ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose the right mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously.    Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML and scientific-computing libraries (PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy).    Strong software engineering skills — you can turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems.    A track record of taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data.    Clear written and verbal communication; able to collaborate effectively across research and engineering disciplines.       Nice to Have     PhD in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, photogrammetry, geodesy, remote sensing, or a related field — not required, but valued.    A strong publication record or active involvement in the research community at venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, SIGGRAPH, 3DV, ICRA, or RSS.    Experience with learning-based approaches for visual or 3D understanding — transformers, point transformers, foundation models, or methods combining learned representations with explicit geometric priors.    Experience with aerial or satellite imagery, GNSS/GPS, geodesy, mapping systems, or large-scale spatial data.    Evidence of technical leadership, mentorship, or successful cross-functional delivery.       Compensation & Benefits   Base salary: Competitive market rate. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.     Location & Work Model   This role is based in our London office, with three days per week in office. We welcome applications from candidates who require visa sponsorship.     Inclusive Application   We know the strongest candidates don't always tick every box. If you're excited about this role and believe you could do it well, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed — you may be exactly who we're looking for.     Equal Opportunity   Niantic Spatial is an equal opportunity employer. Individuals seeking employment at Niantic Spatial are considered without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, age, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or related medical conditions), marital status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other protected category under applicable laws. Niantic Spatial will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in accordance with applicable laws. Please contact your recruiter if you want to request an accommodation for the job application or interview process.     Candidate Privacy   I understand that by submitting my job application, the information I provide as part of that application will be used in accordance with Niantic Spatial's Privacy Notice for Job Applicants and Candidates  https://www.nianticspatial.com/applicant-privacy-notice . job.description: About Kernel   Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?    Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.    Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.    Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent KERN ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at  Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Checkout  already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.    We have raised $14M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 5x YoY.     The Role     We have strong product market fit. In 2025 we grew ~5x with world class net dollar retention, mostly from founder-led sales, and now have AEs hitting quota with an emerging playbook.    We're looking for another BDR Manager to accelerate our outbound engine as we scale in 2026. You'll own a team of ~10 BDRs and be responsible for the pipeline that fuels our growth.    You will report to Dave Bentham (Head of Sales) and work closely with our AEs, marketing, and leadership team to make sure the top of funnel is consistently feeding high-quality pipeline.       What You’ll Be Doing    Set the strategy     Work with Dave and the rest of leadership to define ICP, targeting, and outbound messaging.    Translate company targets into clear, measurable BDR goals and ensure pipeline expectations are distributed strategically across the team.    Continuously iterate on outbound plays, channels, and sequences to improve conversion at every stage.    Develop the BDR team to be a talent pool for the rest of the organisation through a culture of constant learning       Set your team     Manage and develop a team of ~10 BDRs across inbound and outbound.    Work alongside our recruiters to grow the team as we scale.    Be accountable for team performance. Coach underperformers, promote top performers, and set a high bar across the board.    Our BDR team is the talent engine for the entire GTM team. Nurturing the best people and helping them be ready for the next role is crucial.       Set the operating cadence     Define qualification criteria and handoff processes that set AEs up to close.    Build repeatable outbound plays that convert, and partner with marketing where needed.    Establish pipeline generation rigor: activity metrics, and predictable output.    Run weekly team reviews, call coaching sessions, and continuous improvement loops.       What You Bring:     4+ years in business development and/or outbound sales, with at least some time managing a BDR or SDR team.    Experience scaling a BDR team (e.g. growing from a handful of reps to 10+) or managing a team of that size.    Strong instincts for messaging, targeting, and what makes outbound actually work.    Comfort operating in ambiguity: you can build process, playbooks, and territory strategy.    Bonus: the deeper your knowledge of RevOps, data, and GTM tools the better.      ⚠️  This role may not be for you if you:     Need lots of structure or polished specs.    You like spending weeks agonizing on a single initiative, or don’t want to rapidly iterate and run experiments. In a nutshell    Join a fast-growing SaaS company in an international environment (steep learning curve guaranteed). About Kaizo  At Kaizo, we build a performance development and quality platform for customer support teams. Our AutoQA product uses LLMs to review support conversations against each customer's own quality rubric, automatically and at scale. Behind it sits a microservices-based stream processing platform handling over 200 million events per day (Kafka, Kubernetes on Google Cloud, ElasticSearch, MongoDB, BigQuery), and an LLMOps stack built around LangSmith for experimentation, prompt management, and tracing.  The hard part isn't calling an LLM. It's knowing, with evidence, how well the system performs on every customer's unique rubric, and having a reliable, repeatable way to improve it. That's where you come in.    What you'll focus on       Translate customer rubrics into AutoQA instructions.  Work with real customer quality criteria and turn them into precise, testable instructions that LLMs can score reliably.     Run experiments that move accuracy.  Design and execute evaluation experiments on large, representative datasets using LangSmith and BigQuery, and track quality with our performance metrics.     Build the datasets that make evaluation possible.  Curate raw production data into golden datasets with balanced coverage, and generate synthetic data to cover the rare cases that matter most. QA is a discipline of rare occurrences: distributions are skewed, positives are scarce, and resourcefulness beats volume.     Build LLM-as-a-judge pipelines  to assess system quality internally and make evaluation repeatable.     Make results actionable.  Your experiments should end in a decision: change a prompt, adjust which tools the system uses, surface context the AI is missing, or flag where new capabilities are needed. You'll work with the AI team to ship those decisions.     Evaluate across the full stack.  Beyond scoring quality, you'll help validate retrieval (RAG/IR), tool calling, and speech pipelines (transcription and diarization quality).     Join customer calls with the team  to understand how QA leaders define quality, and feed what you learn back into the product.      What you'll grow into    Shaping how customers monitor quality themselves, catch drift, and keep their AutoQA setup improving over time.    Smarter categorization and routing of conversations to power analytics and get the right tickets to the right evaluation.             A solid understanding of how LLMs work and hands-on experience prompting them for accuracy (coursework, thesis, internships, or side projects all count; production experience is a bonus).    Good applied statistics: experiment design, classifier evaluation, precision/recall trade-offs, and working with heavily imbalanced data.    Strong Python skills and fluency with the standard data toolkit (Pandas, NumPy, Jupyter). SQL is a plus.    An analytical, evidence-first mindset: you'd rather measure than assume.    Product sense and empathy for end users. You'll be building for QA managers and support agents, not just for benchmarks.    Excellent written and verbal communication. You'll present findings to the team and join customer conversations.    0 to 2 years of industry experience. Recent graduates with strong relevant work are encouraged to apply.    A team player who's comfortable wearing multiple hats. We're an early-stage company and things move fast.     Bonus points for:     Experience with LangSmith or similar LLMOps/evaluation tooling    Google Cloud Platform, BigQuery, Docker, or Kubernetes    Speech/audio processing or ASR evaluation    Fine-tuning or building synthetic datasets for LLMs      Who you'll work with    You'll join our AI team (two data scientists, an AI engineer, and an ML engineer) and collaborate closely with our data engineers, frontend engineers, designer, product manager, and CX teams. You'll have mentorship from day one and real ownership fast.    What's in it for you? We help companies automate the most critical parts of finance, from closing the books and recognizing revenue to consolidating entities and reporting to investors. More than 600 companies run on Rillet, including Mercor, Scribe, and Function Health, and we partner with leading accounting firms including EY and KPMG.  We’re building in one of the largest software markets in the world, with the momentum to match. Rillet has raised more than $200M, is valued at $1B, and is backed by Sequoia, a16z, ICONIQ, Bain Capital Ventures, Oak HC/FT, and other leading investors. We’re using that backing to build the financial infrastructure for the next generation of companies and help every business run its numbers at the speed of AI.     Who We Are   Rillet’s pace is not for everyone. Intelligence is table stakes. To succeed here, you need extreme speed, agency, and flexibility.  The people who thrive at Rillet do not wait for assignments. They internalize the mission, design a strategy, and bring back results that are better, faster, and more creative than a manager could have asked for.  Our work revolves around our customers. The people who succeed here are energized by delivering what matters most, even when it was not part of the original plan. You do need to care deeply about the problems we solve and the impact our customers can create. Partner with internal teams across Product, Engineering, and Customer Success

job.description: Bij Centric geloven we dat technologie de wereld beter kan maken. Daarom zijn we constant op zoek naar enthousiaste en gedreven professionals zoals jij, die het verschil willen maken. Maak werk van deze mogelijkheden.       Wat jij doet     Als je van uitdagende technische opdrachten binnen het Cloud spectrum houdt, dan past Centric perfect bij jou.       Je duikt in de wereld van Azure, of AWS, bij de ene opdracht werk je bij een financiële instelling en bij de volgende bij een overheidsinstelling. Het kan als Cloud DevOps Engineer bij Centric. Daarnaast bieden wij je de kans om jezelf te blijven ontwikkelen.    Je duikt in de wereld van de Cloud en ontwerpt, implementeert en beheert de CI/CD DevOps pipelines. Hoe je dit doet? Door jouw kennis en ervaring effectief in te zetten bij klanten. Wat doe je onder andere nog meer?      Je ontwerpt, implementeert en automatiseert CI/CD pipelines en maakt hierbij gebruik van infrastructure-as-code      Je denkt en praat mee over source control en branching strategieën      Jouw infrastructure-as-code zorgt ervoor dat de infrastructuur die je uitrolt veilig is en compliant met het beleid van je opdrachtgever      Het zorgen voor het implementeren van beveiligingsprotocollen en compliance standaarden.       Als Cloud DevOps Engineer treed je in dienst bij Centric en word je ingezet bij één of meerdere opdrachtgevers. job.description:
In a nutshell

Join us in designing the future of grocery shopping. As a Product Designer in our consumer team, you'll own the design of our core mobile app, shaping the daily shopping experience for hundreds of thousands of people in The Netherlands, Germany and France. You'll tackle the unique challenge of designing for a task that is frequent, personal, and central to our customers' lives. You'll be part of a dedicated product team and our wider UX Guild, a creative community that ensures a world-class user experience across Picnic. We’re looking for a passionate designer to join our Amsterdam HQ and help build a product people genuinely love, in a fast-scaling environment that values autonomy, collaboration, and adaptability over rigid processes.

Tricks of the trade

  • Have the autonomy to own the design of new features from beginning to end. Everything you do matters and will be developed and tested at a fast pace.
  • Sharpen project briefs based on explorative research together with UX researchers and product owners. 
  • Build low and high fidelity prototypes to be tested and evaluated on a weekly basis with real users.
  • Document the final design requirements on interaction and UI level to brief and support developers during the development phase. 
  • Learn and grow through the continuous feedback and mentoring by seasoned UX designers and researchers. 
  • Support the development and maintenance of our design libraries and system.
  • Continuously explore new ideas in order to initiate new projects and improvements, design is never done ;). 

Your superpowers

  • You have a completed degree in a relevant design field (e.g. CMD, UX, Interaction or Product Design)
  • You have 0-3 years of experience as a UX designer and have worked on or have a strong interest in building great products
  • Your portfolio has user-centered design cases that show your problem solving capabilities
  • You have a deep curiosity to understand our customers and have hands-on experience in exploratory research to discover and define user problems from scratch
  • You know your way around Figma and are able to craft high-fidelity designs that fit into our design system
  • You bring a low-ego, collaborative mindset and enjoy building solutions together

job.description: Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.    The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But International Fintechs and non-US banks are left with two unsatisfying options to access it: Either they build on legacy clearing banks that are slow and unreliable, or they interface with middleware providers that don’t move and hold the dollars directly, but themselves rely on underlying legacy banks. Augustus collapses this stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.   We are a group of operators, unicorn early employees, ex-founders and people who walked away from degrees because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and n8n.   We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.    The Role  You’re a Fellow at Augustus, deployed to special projects across engineering, product, and the wider company. You own a project end to end: understand the problem, decide how to approach it, build the solution, and get it into use.  The work depends on where you can have the most impact. You could build background coding agents, create a frontend component library, or solve an operational problem with agents. The common thread is a meaningful problem, a clear outcome, and ownership of getting it done.  You’ll work closely with the team your project sits in. They provide context, technical guidance, and direct feedback. You bring the drive to turn an open-ended problem into something that works. As you deliver, the scope and difficulty of your projects grow.  Your First Months  Get context quickly, ship early, and take on harder problems as you prove yourself.     Month 1:  Join a team, understand the problem, and take ownership of your first project. Talk to the people who will use what you build, agree on what success looks like, and ship an initial version.     Months 2–3:  Drive the project through to adoption. Work through technical decisions, collect feedback, and improve the solution. You’re becoming more independent and developing better judgment about where to spend your time. The problems you can solve today are meaningfully harder than those you could solve six months ago. You seek feedback and put it to work.     Drive.  You make things happen. You find a way through unfamiliar problems, follow up without being chased, and stay with a project until it works.     Curiosity.  You want to understand how things work and why. You dig into unfamiliar systems, ask precise questions, and look beyond the first plausible answer.     Ownership.  You care about the outcome. You involve the right people, raise blockers early, and check that what you shipped actually solves the problem.     Low ego.  You can defend an idea, change your mind, and commit to a team decision. Able to explain your decisions, ask for help when needed, and follow through. These people will be foundational in your future opportunities.     Real Participation:  Employees are shareholders. You will think and act like an owner.     Perks & Benefits:  Relocation support, visa support, the latest Apple gear (MacBook + AirPods), lunch benefit, gym benefit, a beautiful office in the heart of the city, 4x on-/offsites per year, and an annual development budget.    Additional to the global benefits above, we offer localized benefits such as comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance and a 401(k) retirement plan for our US team. Augustus will consider all applications for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, religious beliefs, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, neurodiversity, disability, age, parental or veteran status. job.description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person.

We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform.

This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch.

We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one.

This role will be based in London, UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin.

What you'll do:

  • Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers.
  • Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout.
  • Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times.
  • Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer.
  • Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter.

job.description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.  About The Exploration Company  At The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable orbital space vehicle that aims to eventually be refuelled in orbit, carrying cargo and potentially humans in the long run. The heart of a spacecraft lies in its engine, which is why we develop our own propulsion systems, aiming for the highest level of efficiency and reliability.    Role Summary  We are seeking a  Junior Engine Control System & Monitoring Engineer  to join the engine control and monitoring team of Storm, our high-thrust LOX/LCH4 cryogenic rocket engine. Working alongside senior control engineers, you will develop and test control and monitoring algorithms, work with the engine functional models provided by the functional team, contribute to setting up the controller development environment, and help verify the controller through Model-, Software- and Hardware-in-the-Loop testing and during engine test campaigns. This is an entry-level, hands-on role for a recent graduate with strong control fundamentals who wants to learn on real hardware and progressively grow into full ownership of safety-critical engine control functions.     Key responsibilities:   1. Control & Monitoring Algorithm Development  • Design and implement engine control and monitoring algorithms, following the software team's rules, guidelines and auto-coding practices.  • Contribute to the definition of the engine regulation strategy (thrust and mixture ratio control, chill-down, start-up and shutdown transients) together with functional and system engineers.  • Support the definition of control and monitoring requirements for engine subsystems (valves, pumps, sensors, controller, software).    2. Simulation & Controller Development Environment  • Contribute to setting up the controller development environment: toolchain, model and code configuration management, auto-coding chain, and the MiL/SiL/HiL simulation and test infrastructure.  • Integrate the engine functional models delivered by the functional team (turbopumps, valves, combustion devices, cryogenic feed lines; steady-state, transient and chill-down) into the control design and simulation environment, deriving simplified or linearised models for controller synthesis where needed.  • Run closed-loop simulations to assess controller performance, stability margins and robustness to model uncertainties.  • Feed test results back to the functional team to support model correlation, and flag model limitations that matter for control.    3. Health Monitoring & Fault Management  • Contribute to the engine monitoring strategy that assesses the health status of the engine and its subsystems (combustion chamber, turbopumps, valves…).  • Implement fault detection and sensor validation logic for both real-time protection and post-test analysis.  • Support failure mode analyses (FMEA) and the management of failure modes, paving the way for engine reusability.    4. Validation, Testing & Documentation  • Prepare and run Model-, Software- and Hardware-in-the-Loop (MiL, SiL, HiL) test campaigns to verify the control and monitoring functions at each step, from Simulink model to embedded code on target hardware.  • Support Storm engine and component cryogenic (LOX/LCH4) test campaigns: test preparation, on-site support, data processing and post-test analysis.  • Produce clear development documentation: specifications, test procedures, test reports and justification files.     What we would love to see from you:   • Master's degree (or equivalent) in Aerospace, Electrical, Control or Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.  • Recent graduate (or graduating within the next months); no professional experience required. A master's thesis, internship or academic project in control, propulsion or embedded systems is a strong plus.  • Solid fundamentals in control theory, both classical and modern (state-space, robustness, digital control).  • Practical use of MATLAB/Simulink and Python through coursework or projects; basic knowledge of C/C++.  • Basic understanding of fluid dynamics and thermodynamics, and a strong interest in cryogenic propulsion and turbomachinery.  • Fluent in English.    Nice to Have:   • Exposure to MiL/SiL/HiL testing or real-time embedded systems.  • Experience with auto-coding from Simulink models.  • Familiarity with safety-critical design practices, reliability engineering or failure mode analysis.  • Interest or experience in data science applied to health monitoring and anomaly detection.  • Knowledge of space standards (ECSS, MIL-STD, NASA-HBK…).  • German and/or French.    Skills & Behaviours:  • Eagerness to learn and to take on increasing ownership under the guidance of senior engineers.  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to draw useful conclusions from partial or contradictory data.  • Clear oral and written communication; comfortable working closely with engine, avionics, software and test teams.  • Organised, able to prioritise tasks and deliver within time constraints.  • Positive, flexible attitude and enthusiasm for space exploration.  • Behaviour consistent with The Exploration Company's core values of Mission, Vision, Integrity, Excellence and Teamwork.   Why you should join us!   What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:      We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind     We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them      We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?      We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly.     The Exploration Company is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status. Relocation assistance is provided for those willing to relocate including visa sponsorship where applicable.       All offers are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, which will be subject to the country, role, and project you applied for. By submitting your application, you acknowledge and agree that any offer of employment may be conditional upon successful condition of this check. The Exploration Company partners with Zinc Work Limited located in the UK (Zinc), a third-party provider, to ensure this process as efficient and transparent as possible.   If applicable, you will receive an email from Zinc upon acceptance of your offer with a link to a secure portal where you can provide the required information to Zinc. job.description: About the Role   Imagine pioneering the mathematical and logical foundations that enable AI to fly safely in real-world, safety-critical aviation. As a Machine Learning Certification Researcher, you will address one of the most fundamental challenges in modern AI: proving that ML models are safe, reliable, and mathematically sound for deployment in autonomous flight. Your work will bridge the gap between cutting-edge statistical learning theory and formal aviation certification frameworks, building upon previous work (EASA CoDANN I and II, and FAA report DOT/FAA/TC-21/48), and putting real-world systems to the test.  At Destinus, we are shaping the future of defense through high-speed, autonomous flight technologies. We develop next-generation unmanned aerial systems that deliver greater speed, precision, and efficiency, supporting governments and defense organizations in mission-critical operations worldwide. Daedalean AG, the AI and autonomy hub of the Destinus Group, plays a key role in this vision—developing safety-critical AI systems at the intersection of advanced research and real-world aviation. Enabling machines to perceive, understand, and make decisions in real time, we combine aerospace engineering and artificial intelligence to build the next generation of autonomous flight systems, driving innovation where it matters most.   What You'll Do   • AI Certification Strategy: Analyze our existing AI certification strategy and help adapt it—or pioneer entirely new strategies—to certify different supervised ML.  • EASA Framework Alignment: Connect mathematical guarantees, technical arguments, and model evaluations to the EASA W-shaped process for AI certification in aviation, ensuring our research aligns with the latest regulatory guidelines.  • Theoretical Foundation & Modeling: Conduct research into statistical learning theory, generalization bounds, and mathematical guarantees for deep neural networks operating under dynamic real-world conditions.  • Uncertainty Quantification: Apply statistics and stochastic processes to model environmental uncertainties and sensor noise, and to quantify confidence in performance metrics.  • Literature & Proof Evaluation: Critically evaluate academic literature, mathematical proofs, and engineering assumptions with peer-review rigor to identify safety limitations and theoretical gaps in state-of-the-art AI.  • Regulatory & Audit Justification: Construct robust, logical arguments and technical justifications that translate complex, high-dimensional empirical data into structured evidence for safety audits and certification frameworks.  • Algorithmic Validation: Write clean, reproducible code in Python to test theoretical hypotheses, validate certification mechanisms, and benchmark model safety frameworks.   Requirements    What You'll Need    Machine Learning Theory & Mathematics   • ML Theory & Statistical Learning: Deep understanding of statistical learning theory, generalization bounds, and the math

Cela inclura l’utilisation de vos compétences techniques et votre expérience de vente consultative pour recruter d’excellentes personnes en première ligne de management et contributeurs individuels, établir des processus pour évoluer votre équipe, et représenter Anthropic directement dans les engagements clients stratégiques. About the Role:

As the 2nd-line leader for the Applied AI Industries team in Southern Europe and the Middle-East at Anthropic, you will drive the adoption of frontier AI in partnership with the rest of the go to market organization. Our Industries customers in France, Iberia and Italy include many of the region's largest enterprises across financial services, healthcare and life sciences, manufacturing, telecom, retail, energy, and other sectors. You'll leverage your experience building and leading technical sales teams to drive positive AI transformation that addresses our customers' business needs, meets their technical and regulatory requirements, and provides a high degree of reliability and safety.

 

You will be responsible for leading and growing the solutions architect team that partners with account executives to help companies adopt and deploy Anthropic's products, including Claude Cowork, Claude Code, and the Claude Development Platform (our API). This will include leveraging your technical skills and consultative sales experience to hire great 1st line managers and individual contributors, establish processes to scale your team, and represent Anthropic directly at strategic customer engagements. Your team covers several countries and industries at once, so you will be responsible for thinking strategically about complex industry accounts and for identifying and rolling out solutions that resonate in each market, with its own language, business culture, and regulatory context.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Hire, manage, and guide a team of 1st line managers who will in turn build teams of pre-sales Applied AI Architects across France, Iberia and Italy.

  • Set goals for your team in collaboration with sales leadership and establish baseline expectations for performance across your team.

  • Act as a technical and executive sponsor for high-value strategic customers in the region and advise them on their overall AI adoption strategies or use case scoping and pilot execution.

  • Partner closely with Southern Europe sales leadership (also covering the Middle-East and Africa) to build strategies for complex industry accounts and identify new ways to drive adoption of Anthropic products within specific verticals or horizontal use cases.

  • Help customers navigate local and European regulatory requirements (for example the EU AI Act, GDPR, DORA, and data residency expectations) and adapt how your team engages to the business culture of each market.

  • Work with cross-functional teams like product and engineering to ensure Anthropic prioritizes customer feedback or resolves blockers to adoption in the region.

  • Travel regularly across Southern Europe to customers or conferences for executive-level sessions, technical workshops, and relationship building.

  • Establish a shared vision for creating solutions that enable beneficial and safe AI in technology products.

  • Contribute to thought leadership through conference presentations, webinars, and technical content creation.

  • Stay current with emerging AI trends and the competitive landscape.

 

You may be a good fit if you:

  • 7+ years of technical pre-sales management experience, including 2nd-line leadership or above (leading managers).

  • Have sold complex technical products to large enterprises in France, Iberia, Italy, the Middle-East and Africa.

  • Have worked across multiple industries, such as financial services, healthcare and life sciences, manufacturing, telecom, retail, and energy.

  • Understand the cultural differences between Southern European markets and the regulatory context your customers operate in, and adapt your approach to each.

  • Think highly strategically about complex industry accounts, and turn that thinking into plans your team and sales counterparts can execute.

  • Have deep technical proficiency with enterprise AI use cases, API integrations, and LLM deployments.

  • Thrive in building and rapidly scaling teams and processes within ambiguous and fast-moving environments.

  • Have excellent communication, collaboration, and coaching abilities.

  • Strong executive presence and ability to foster deep relationships with business and technical leaders at the region's largest companies.

  • Have at least a high level familiarity with the architecture and operation of LLMs.

  • Have a passion for making powerful technology safe and societally beneficial.

  • Stay up-to-date and informed by taking an active interest in emerging research and industry trends within AI.

 

Strong candidates may have:

  • Enterprise pre-sales leadership at scale: 5+ years leading solution architect teams through hypergrowth (ideally dozens of people across several countries), with direct experience leading managers and developing talent in complex enterprise software sales environments.

  • Multilingual and multicultural range: In addition to English, fluency in one or more of French, Italian, Spanish or Portuguese, and experience leading teams distributed across several countries.

  • Experience with consumption business models: Ideal candidates have built GTM frameworks anchored on consumption, not just SaaS-based licenses.

  • AI Technical Depth + Executive Engagement: Hands-on experience with AI platforms and enterprise integration patterns, combined with proven track record engaging C-level stakeholders in €10M+ technical evaluations and enterprise sales cycles.

  • Multi-industry GTM experience in regulated sectors: Demonstrated success adapting technical approaches to different verticals, in particular regulated ones such as banking, insurance, and healthcare, including working with risk, compliance, and works council stakeholders.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
€265.000—€310.000 EUR

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you ----- addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. job.description: Company Description     We’re        Checkout.com   . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.      We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.     Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.     If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.     With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.     About the team  Our Sanctions Screening team keeps our merchants and their customers safe. We run and constantly improve the real-time screening that checks payments and customers against sanctions and watchlists. We're scaling it fast as we move into new markets and payment types.    The role  This is an associate-level role for a sharp, hands-on data analyst. You'll help with the day-to-day running and improvement of our screening systems, making them faster, more accurate and more resilient. Sanctions screening, compliance and fincrime experience is a plus, not a must.   Strong data analysts from adjacent payments, fintech or similar fields are welcome to apply.    What you'll do    Support the day-to-day running of our screening platform (Fircosoft Continuity, the system that checks payments and customers against watchlists), keeping it healthy and reliable.    Design and test rules that cut false positives and reduce manual case work.    Manage watchlist updates and configurations to stay ahead of regulatory change.    Extend screening to new payment types and build automated testing so improvements stick.      What success looks like    False positives and manual workload fall measurably, without weakening detection.    Screening runs reliably and no longer depends on any single person.    New payment types and controls are supported quickly as the business grows.      What you'll bring    2–3 years' experience in a data analyst or data-focused role.    Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. You turn data into decisions.    Hands-on data skills with SQL/BigQuery and/or Python. Comfort in a fast-moving, high-performance and high-growth environment.      Nice to have    Experience in sanctions screening, AML, fraud or transaction monitoring.    Experience configuring screening tools

Je voelt je prettig wanneer een vraagstuk nog open is en weet onderzoek om te zetten in concrete vervolgstappen.      Daarnaast:      Je hebt 3+ jaar ervaring als Product Designer, UX Designer of UX/UI Designer en hebt digitale producten ontworpen en opgeleverd in een multidisciplinair team. job.description:
About CreativeX

CreativeX is B2B SaaS technology platform that helps global marketing teams make smarter creative decisions and elevate creative expression through the clarity of data. Our technology powers creative decision-making at some of the biggest brands in the world, including Google, Unilever, Pepsi, Bayer, Mondelez, Heineken, and more.

We use computer vision and other machine learning techniques to extract creative data from our client's digital advertising copy and transform those previously dark signals into a standardised data model at industrial scale. This creates a new, unique and powerful first party data set that represents the last and most impactful untapped reservoir of advertising performance.

That's because multiple studies have shown that the "Creative" itself is responsible for half of sales lift online, higher than reach, targeting, brand, & recency combined. But creative impact has always been the least analysed and least understood component of a complex set of marketing variables.

This is the problem CreativeX is focussed on solving. We're an end-to-end solution to ingest, process, and analyse content at scale. We help brands isolate creative elements so they can be analysed against downstream ad impact metrics, from clickthrough rates to brand lift.

Our objective is to help marketing organisations power every creative decision with data.

Product Design Team

As a Product Designer, you'll help shape the next generation of the CreativeX platform, taking problems from discovery through to shipped experiences across defined areas of the product. You'll be the design lead in a product trio alongside a Product Manager and an Engineering Lead, owning whether users want what we build and whether they can figure out how to use it, while sharing discovery, outcomes and trade-offs with your partners. CreativeX is a complex product with rich data, multiple user types and increasingly sophisticated AI capabilities, and as AI increases the volume and speed of creative production, you'll make that complexity work for marketers, helping them measure performance fast, find the patterns behind what's working and see whether their full set of ads is delivering the strategy. Our roadmap is framed as problems to solve, not screens to make, so we expect you to bring a point of view. Product Design is a small, hands-on team in a scale-up: you'll be trusted with real ownership early, and this hire is an important step in growing the team.

What you will do

  • Own design for defined product areas, from understanding the problem through to working with Product and Engineering to ship the right experience
  • Get close to marketers and creative teams through customer conversations, research and usability testing, using what you learn to inform design decisions
  • Partner with Product and Engineering in discovery

job.description: Scope   automates the data collection that's slowing down the physical world.  Standards are vital for the safety of our infrastructure. Spending hours manually documenting them is not.  Dave is an inspector. Today he's climbing through one of Europe's biggest chemical plants, looking for the corrosion that could shut the whole site down, with a notebook and pen in hand. Tomorrow, he'll spend even longer on the part of the job he hates: turning those scribbles into a report.  We're building the best AI-native data collection layer for the 2 billion field workers like Dave. Scope radically simplifies how inspectors collect data in the field, make decisions, and produce reports. Along the way, we're building the world's largest dataset on the condition of the built world and the decisions experts make about it.  It's a $2T market and we're just getting started, with ambitions. We work with 6 of the top 10 companies in the space. Our customers inspect facilities and products for companies including AstraZeneca and SpaceX.  We've assembled a best-in-class team: acquired and future founders, people from institutions like Imperial, Carnegie Mellon and Oxford, and from firms like Goldman Sachs, Flexport and Amazon.  Since launching from Entrepreneurs First in 2024, we've raised an oversubscribed $20m round led by   Index Ventures  , the firm behind Figma, Revolut and Wiz, with 100+ unicorns backed to date.     About the role   We're hiring our first Product Designer.  Every engineer at Scope is a product engineer: they talk to users, decide what to build and ship it themselves. You'll work the same way, with design as your edge, and help the engineers around you to build a better product. That covers the whole experience, not just the surface: which problem we solve, how the flow works, what happens when things go wrong, and how it all looks. You'll work closely with the engineers, with Ish our Product Manager, and with Jakob the CTO.  We work in person five days a week from our office in Farringdon.     What you'll work on   Some examples of surfaces in our product that will need your help:    Our mobile app gets used inside tanks and on top of pressure vessels. People wear thick gloves, there's usually no signal, and one hand is often holding on to something. Most of what makes a normal app pleasant doesn't apply there, so a big part of the job is figuring out what does.    Then there's the report. How AI and the inspector will work together to produce 40 page reports and review them is something nobody has designed well yet.    Inspectors but also decision makers should be able to ask things like "Which tanks were over the corrosion limit last year?". Sometimes the right interface will be a chat but often it isn't. job.description: About the Role   There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.  Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. We believe products will greatly reduce hallucinations  Our objective is to organise anyone's life, allowing us all to spend time on valuable and meaningful things  As Product Lead, AI Email App, you work at the intersection of user needs, model capability, and engineering constraints. You will work directly with ML and engineering teams to define how the system should behave, how we measure it, and how we continuously improve it.  This is a deeply technical, hands-on role. You are expected to understand the system and challenge technical decisions.     What You'll Own     Define end-to-end requirements for AI capabilities, from model behavior to system behavior to user experience.    Translate model capabilities, evaluation results, and technical constraints into clear product and system decisions.    Make trade-offs across quality, latency, cost, reliability, safety, and UX.    Work closely with ML, backend, and client engineers on system design, evaluation, and iteration.    Define and evolve evaluation frameworks across offline metrics, online experiments, and human feedback.    Establish clear quality bars and feedback loops for AI-powered experiences.    Drive execution through clear specifications, prioritization, and strong technical judgment.    Identify failure modes and ensure AI systems behave predictably and recover gracefully.    Own product quality end-to-end, correctness, reliability, usefulness, and user trust.       What We're Looking For      Technical     Strong computer science fundamentals and system design skills.    Solid understanding of modern ML and how AI systems behave in production.    Comfortable reading technical designs, understanding architectures, and engaging deeply with engineers.    Strong intuition for model limitations, hallucinations, evaluation, and failure modes.       Product & AI     Significant experience owning complex, technical products end-to-end.    Hands-on experience with AI-powered products, particularly LLM-based systems.    Experience with model evaluation, experimentation, prompting, or AI system iteration.    Ability to turn ambiguous problems into clear requirements, measurable outcomes, and executable plans.    Strong judgment and the ability to make decisions when the right answer is not obvious.       Mindset     Highly technical, curious, and comfortable going deep.    Strong bias toward shipping, experimentation, and learning from real-world usage. job.title: Product Manager

job.description:
Product Manager - Agent Experience 

Location: Paris, France preferred, open to London applicants (hybrid, three days a week in the office)
Team: Customer care
Salary: €46,000 – €55,000 / £47,000 – £59,000
Language: Fluency in French & English
Contract: Permanent 
Reporting To: Lead Product Manager

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the EU. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.

About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

What you’ll do

  • Own the Roadmap: Lead the end-to-end strategy for Kaluza Agent Experience (KAE) within the European market—grounded in global product goals but sharpened by local client needs and agent behaviors. Driving core operational metrics (AHT, FCR, CSAT, AI adoption, onboarding)ensuring capabilities improve agent/customer outcomes.
  • Drive Journey Design & UX Consistency: Act as guardian of agent UX across KAE to ensure coherence across the experience. Partnering with UX and domain teams to apply shared patterns consistently, reduce agent cognitive load, and maintain alignment and compliance with the design system as new automation and assistive/AI capabilities are introduced.
  • Lead Integrations & Client Onboarding: Drive technical and product integrations with third-party platforms and oversee spinning up new KAE instances end-to-end for incoming clients from discovery through go-live.
  • Ensure Accessibility & Compliance: Champion EU accessibility regulations by design, translating regulatory and market-specific needs into actionable engineering requirements.
  • Engage Clients & Drive Value: Serve as the trusted expert for clients on agent experience, advocating for platform-first configuration over bespoke builds
  • Hands-on Delivery & Enablement: Maintain active involvement across the entire Product Development Life Cycle (PDLC)—from agent discovery sessions to feedback loops—and produce materials to support successful client adoption.

    (Note: Travel to client sites e.g., Brussels, is expected at roughly 1–3 trips a month initially, tapering to 1–2 times a quarter.)

What you’ll bring

Ideally, you’ll have:

  • Contact Centre & UX Expertise: Deep experience owning end-to-end user journeys for high-frequency operational tools (e.g., agent desktops), with hands-on craft in user research, journey mapping, and usability testing with agents and supervisors.
  • EU Accessibility & Platform Integration: Strong working knowledge of EU accessibility standards alongside proven experience integrating products with complex third-party platforms and vendor ecosystems.
  • Client Delivery & Market Expansion: Successful track record implementing or localizing a product for external enterprise clients, taking solutions from zero to live through discovery, configuration, and change management.
  • Data-Informed Judgement & Influence: Demonstrated ability using operational metrics (AHT, FCR, CSAT, agent effort) to defend product decisions, coupled with a platform-first mindset that prioritizes existing capabilities over custom code.
  • Bilingual Capability: Full professional bilingual fluency (written and spoken) in both English and French.

What will set you apart 

  • Experience leveraging AI tools, machine learning capabilities, or LLM integrations within product workflows to enhance platform intelligence and automation directly into customer service desktop environments.
  • Prior experience within SaaS platforms, the energy sector, or large-scale utility migrations.
  • Hands-on experience to scale UI consistency across different product teams.
  • Hands-on experience to scale UI consistency across different product teams.

Where you'll work
We offer flexible working, with an expectation of 3 days a week in the office. This gives us the best of both: real time together to collaborate and build relationships, with the flexibility to work in the way that suits you best the rest of the week.

Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.
  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.
  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.
  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.
    Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

Our Perks

  • Financial & Insurance: Discretionary bonus, Alan Mutuelle Health Insurance, x3 Life & Death insurance (Prévoyance) via Alan, and standard Sécurité Sociale contributions (pension, family allowance, unemployment insurance)
  • Allowances: 50% commuting expense reimbursement, €200 Home Working Allowance, and €150 Learning Fund
  • Time Off & Flexibility: 25 days holiday + bank holidays + RTT days, Moments That Matter Leave, Compassionate Leave, two paid Volunteering Days, Flexible Working, and Career Break eligibility

We want the best people
We’re keen to meet people from all walks of life — our view is that the more inclusive we are, the better our work will be. We want to build teams which represent a variety of experiences, perspectives and skills, and we recognise talent on the basis of merit and potential.

Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

job.description: Few people get to build a bank from scratch. Even fewer get to build one at a moment when banking itself is being reinvented.    The Dollar is the best product in the history of the world - there is infinite global demand. But International Fintechs and non-US banks are left with two unsatisfying options to access it: Either they build on legacy clearing banks that are slow and unreliable, or they interface with middleware providers that don’t move and hold the dollars directly, but themselves rely on underlying legacy banks. Augustus collapses this stack by combining two things: A real, national bank charter (in organization), and Marble, our proprietary core banking system, built around intelligence, made of code.   We are a group of operators, unicorn early employees, ex-founders and people who walked away from degrees because they believe this is an industry and career defining opportunity. We are backed with more than $200M from Peter Thiel's Valar Ventures, Tiger Global, Hummingbird, QED, Creandum, and the founders of Nubank, Ramp, Deel, Circle, Fluidstack, Fuse, and n8n.   We are regulated in Europe and live with Euro and Stablecoin clearing today. Now, we are building the US team from the ground up, while continuing to grow rapidly in Europe.     The Role   You own Banking Experience: the accounts at the center of customer's relationship with the bank, and the  API and dashboards they use to manage them.  In this role you’re responsible for redefining what beautiful software in banking looks like. You'll define account structures that give customers powerful building blocks for their products, and craft intuitive interfaces grounded in a deep understanding of their use cases and workflows.  You report to Will, Head of Product, and work closely with Simon, our CTO. You're expected to operate with full autonomy on your team's roadmap, collaborating with design and engineering.     Your First Six Months      Months 1-2:  Take over day-to-day ownership of the Banking Experience team - the roadmap, the ways of working, the hard decisions. Establish yourself with customers and how they use our accounts. You define and ship your first project.     Months 3-4:  Execution mode. You're unblocking engineering daily, making hard prioritization calls, and shipping your roadmap to customers. You're proactively raising the bar across accounts, API, and dashboard by feeding what you learn from customers into the product.     Months 5-6:  You're working with live customers on the products you've built. Deposits and number of account holders are scaling. You've moved from execution to platform mode - evolving the roadmap based on what our customers are building on top of Augustus.       Who Will Thrive At Augustus   We believe that throwing smart people with high agency at big problems produces the best outcomes. We’re building a modern correspondent bank, and we win by having a better team. The people who succeed here share the following traits:     American Dream:  You’d rather shoot for gold than settle for mediocrity. You pick the harder goal and stay optimistic when the odds are against you. If it feels easy, we aimed too low.     Live Player:  You don’t need permission. You rebuild what’s broken without being asked, challenge how things are done, and move before the perfect moment.     Ever to Excel:  You can’t accept good enough and you take your work personally. When it matters, you do what it takes and keep raising the bar for yourself and your team.     Genuine:  You play for the company, not your title or turf. Low ego, low drama, no politics. You say it straight, also upwards and always assume good intent.     This role is for you if:     You want to spend time with customers to intimately understand and then innovate on their workflows.    You’re a structured and relentless problem solver.    You combine first-principles thinking with deep domain knowledge to make complex processes simple.    You have taste and care deeply about the quality of what you build.    You leverage AI to push the boundaries of what a PM can do.    You’re excited about building a programmable bank and helping shape what that means.       Hard Requirements     Experience end-to-end owning and building banking, fintech, or developer platform products.    Technical enough to spar on architectural decisions with engineers - you're comfortable in API design discussions, not just UI reviews.    You have experience with control planes, dashboards, or console products at infrastructure, finance, or developer tools companies.    You have strong opinions on information architecture and how to organize complex products so they feel simple    Comfortable in customer-facing roles - you've pitched, demoed, and closed early adopters yourself.    Based in New York or Berlin, or willing to relocate.       Pay transparency   Compensation packages at Augustus include base salary, equity, and benefits. New hire offers are made based on a candidate's experience, expertise and geographic location. The annual US base salary range for this role is $180,000-$230,000 + equity.     What We Offer      Career Growth:  You will be given more responsibility and pushed to grow faster than ever before.     Network:  Your peers are brilliant, highly motivated people. These people will be foundational in your future opportunities.     Real Participation:  Employees are shareholders. You will think and act like an owner.     Perks & Benefits:  Relocation support, visa support, the latest Apple gear (MacBook + AirPods), lunch benefit, gym benefit, a beautiful office in the heart of the city, 4x on-/offsites per year, and an annual development budget.    Additional to the global benefits above, we offer localized benefits such as comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance and a 401(k) retirement plan for our US team.     Augustus is committed to creating an inclusive environment where people from all backgrounds can thrive and where different viewpoints and experiences are valued and respected. Augustus will consider all applications for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, national origin, religious beliefs, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, neurodiversity, disability, age, parental or veteran status.   • Translate French market requirements into clear specifications — turn the rules of the French energy market (including how device and meter data flows between grid operators and suppliers) into detailed product requirements covering compliance, data flows and data quality.
  • Build close working relationships — work hand in hand with key partners in the French market to understand their needs, shape requirements together, and build the kind of trusted relationship where they come to you first, using that closeness to steer what we build next for France.
  • Build, don't just specify. Go from idea to working prototype yourself — query data, sketch API contracts, and stand up proofs of concept. We expect you to use AI tooling (e.g. Claude Code) as a daily multiplier to prototype, investigate, and unblock, not just to draft documents.
  • Align global and local teams across all functions — partner closely with engineering, UX, QA and more, with full-stack influence, keeping everyone pointed at the right outcomes. Be the go-to person for this product area in France, and act as the link between our global and local teams to inform priorities and strategy.

About You

Ideally you'll have/be:

  • Proven experience as a Product Manager, Business Analyst, or equivalent role in software companies, with a strong track record of successfully localising complex software products for international markets
  • Previous experience in the French energy industry — you know how the market works and its key players (e.g. Enedis / GRDF), especially around device data and market flows. Experience with energy management or utility platforms in the French market is a strong plus.
  • Fluent in French and very comfortable in English — our platform and many of our teams operate in English, so you move easily between both.
  • Confident working directly with clients — you can run a working session with client stakeholders, draw out the real requirement behind the ask, and keep senior people aligned and brought in.
  • A builder's mentality — resourceful and hands-on, comfortable building a working prototype rather than waiting for the perfect specification.
  • Technically comfortable — at ease with data and data models, databases, and APIs, and able to prototype with modern AI tooling. You don't need to be an engineer, but you think like one and can hold your own in a technical conversation. Equally happy reasoning about a data model and about what the end user sees on screen.
  • A clear, sharp communicator — able to cut through noise and articulate technical and market complexity to a range of stakeholders, including clients.
  • Experience collaborating across cross-functional teams — engineering, QA, BA, Programme, Delivery etc — to deliver localised solutions.
  • Proficiency in AI tools throughout all stages of the product lifecycle — from discovery and ideation to delivery and iteration.
