Product Manager - Products and Pricing

Location: London, UK (hybrid, three days a week in the office)
Salary: £50,000 – £60,000
Team: Energy Commerce
Contract: Permanent 

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.

About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

What you’ll do

  • Lead the localisation efforts for our products and pricing capabilities, ensuring they meet the specific commercial, regulatory, market, and cultural requirements of retailers in Europe.  This will include European localisations such as indexation and unbundled energy products as well as broader market promotions and discounts.
  • Deep dive into European energy market structures and regulations for designated countries, translating complex needs into detailed product specifications.  Understand the broader context of piercing and selling products in Europe and the required tooling, workflows and models to accelerate our retailers
  • Collaborate intensely with clients and in-country experts to understand their unique needs and requirements. You will be the first point of contact with the client for all domain specific needs.
  • Coordinate cross domain discovery and delivery for features that support key journeys, aligning requirements where needed (eg. billing, quoting and energy insights).
  • Define and manage detailed product requirements for features related to country-specific needs to support energy products and pricing.
  • Contribute to the Global Energy Commerce roadmap, when new acceleration opportunities are identified.
  • Work closely with engineering, UX, and QA teams to ensure the successful implementation and testing of localised billing functionalities.
  • Act as the go-to expert for global teams on specific European market nuances related to energy products and pricing and related customer journeys.

    (Note: Travel to client sites e.g., Brussels, is expected at roughly 1–3 trips a month initially, tapering to 1–2 times a quarter.)

What you’ll bring

Ideally, you’ll have:

  • Proven experience as a Product Manager with a strong track record of successfully localising complex software products for international markets.
  • Able to establish and maintain great relationships with B2B clients, throughout the entire product lifecycle.
  • Solid understanding of the end-to-end energy lifecycle within a European context, with a particular focus on retailer commercial operations.
  • Direct experience with specific European energy markets, understanding their unique regulatory frameworks and requirements
  • Exceptional ability to translate abstract regulatory text or client requirements into clear, actionable requirements for development teams.
  • Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams (engineering, legal, operations, client success) to deliver localised solutions.
  • Experience working alongside multiple services/domains to deliver complex journeys.
  • Excellent communication skills, able to articulate technical and market complexities to various stakeholders, including clients.

What will set you apart 

  • Deep, hands-on experience with the French or Belgian energy retail markets, particularly concerning their energy products and pricing specificities.
  • Proficiency in a second European language relevant to key target markets (e.g., French).
  • Experience with large-scale data migration and integration projects involving legacy billing systems.
  • A background in energy commercial operations or regulatory affairs within a European energy retailer.

Where you'll work
We offer flexible working, with an expectation of 3 days a week in the office. This gives us the best of both: real time together to collaborate and build relationships, with the flexibility to work in the way that suits you best the rest of the week.

Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.
  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.
  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.
  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.
    Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

Our Perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period
  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests
  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work
  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget
  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app

We want the best people
We’re keen to meet people from all walks of life — our view is that the more inclusive we are, the better our work will be. We want to build teams which represent a variety of experiences, perspectives and skills, and we recognise talent on the basis of merit and potential.

Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

job.description: About Peec AI  Peec AI is a Berlin-based Series A startup building analytics and intelligence tools for modern SEO and growth teams. As AI reshapes how people discover information online, companies need new ways to understand where they appear, how they perform, and where the next growth opportunities lie. Peec AI helps teams track their visibility across AI search, measure performance, and uncover opportunities to grow their organic presence in an increasingly complex search landscape.    About the role  We're looking for a second Product Marketing Manager to help shape how Peec AI shows up in the world. You'll work side by side with our founding PMM, who sets the positioning and messaging foundation, and your job is to make that foundation work everywhere it needs to: in a sales pitch, a customer conversation, a launch, a competitive deal. You'll work closely with Growth, Product, Sales, and CX, turning what Peec does into stories and materials that customers understand and teams actually use.    What you'll do    Work with our founding PMM to sharpen and evolve positioning and messaging, and own how it gets applied across segments, use cases, and conversations so every audience hears a narrative that is sharp, specific, and credible    Get deep into the product and stay exceptionally close to customers, turning that proximity into insight that’s reflected in everything we say.    Turn product launches and the ongoing drumbeat of releases into the materials teams need to explain and sell them: pitch narratives, decks, one-pagers, battlecards, and demo stories.    Make sure what we create gets used: train Sales and CX teams, join customer calls, see what works in real conversations, and fix what doesn’t.    Run win/loss and buyer research with Sales and CX, and turn what you hear into findings that shape our messaging and inform the roadmap.    Build and maintain competitive intelligence in a category that moves weekly, keeping the team clear-eyed on what is real and what is noise.    Refine our ICP and segment definitions, bringing what you learn from the field into how we talk about who we serve.      What we're looking for    You write with a point of view and hold your opinions loosely. Your drafts argue for something, and you change your mind when the evidence says to.    You’re exceptionally curious about the product, the category, and especially the customer. You ask good questions, listen carefully, and spot things others miss.    You get technical products. You can explain an analytics tool clearly, demo it with confidence, and hold your own with a technical buyer.    You take ownership, bring your own ideas, and are as comfortable leading projects as you are running with someone else’s brief.    4+ years in B2B SaaS product marketing, with a demonstrated history of working with sales and enablement teams. job.description: About us   Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort,   Photoroom   is the leading visual solution for e-commerce.  We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API.  We're a team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide.    Role Summary  We're looking for a  Product ML Engineer  to join one of our product experience teams — SMB, Scaler or Enterprise — and own the ML side of short, high-impact projects.  You'll work on focused ML problems with a clear product outcome, sometimes fine-tuning one of our models, sometimes integrating the best externally available model, but always choosing the fastest and most effective path to customer value.  You'll bring the technical depth of an Applied Scientist while operating with the pace and pragmatism of a product engineer. You'll own the journey from framing the problem through to shipping, measuring and iterating on the feature in production.   This is not a research role.  Your time horizon is weeks rather than quarters, and success is measured by what reaches users and the impact it creates.   About the role     Embed directly within a product team.  Work closely with the SMB, Scaler or Enterprise team on focused ML problems tied to clear customer and business outcomes.     Own ML projects end to end.  Frame the problem, choose the approach, execute the plan, ship the feature and monitor its performance in production.     Make the build vs. buy decision.  Determine when to fine-tune or build a model yourself versus integrating an external model, API or existing library.     Move from idea to production quickly.  Work on projects scoped in weeks rather than quarters, prioritising rapid iteration and customer impact.     Work closely with the ML team.  Leverage shared infrastructure, evaluation tooling and expertise while remaining embedded in the product team's priorities and cadence.     Stay close to users.  Get rapid feedback from customers, monitor how people use what you've shipped and use those insights to drive the next iteration.     Balance technical depth with pragmatism.  Know when deeper modelling work is necessary and when an existing solution is already good enough to ship.     Write production code.  Work directly in the product team's codebase rather than operating primarily through research notebooks and experiments.     Own quality in production.  Build sound evaluations, monitor performance and investigate failures once the feature is live.     About You     You've shipped ML into production.  You have 2+ years of hands-on experience building and shipping ML-powered products, with strong experience in PyTorch or equivalent frameworks such as TensorFlow or JAX.     You have applied-science depth.  You can fine-tune vision or diffusion models, design meaningful evaluations and debug training runs when necessary.     You're a pragmatic builder.  You care about solving the customer's problem rather than proving that your own model is the best approach. You'll happily use an external model, API or existing library when that's the fastest route to value.     You're product-minded.  You measure success through shipped features, user behaviour and business outcomes rather than papers or benchmarks alone.     You're comfortable in production codebases.  You can move between experimentation and production engineering, writing maintainable code that lives inside a real product.     You have strong ownership.  You're comfortable taking an ambiguous ML problem, deciding what matters, choosing an approach and driving it through to production.     You iterate quickly.  You enjoy short feedback loops and would rather ship something useful, learn from users and improve it than spend months optimising something that hasn't reached production.     You're curious and collaborative.  You can both explain your expertise and learn from the deep technical expertise around you. You value knowledge sharing and humility.     You're fluent in English.  French isn't required.     Nice to have:  experience shipping generative image models or diffusion models into production; experience evaluating third-party AI APIs against internal alternatives; experience working in a fast-growing startup or directly within a product team.   Benefits    Competitive salary + meaningful equity    Hybrid working from our Paris headquarters    Visa sponsorship and relocation support up to €10,000    MacBook Pro and full home office setup    30 days annual leave    Private healthcare    Regular company off-sites and team retreats    International English-speaking team    Language lessons in English and French     Hiring Process    Screening with an ML Researcher / Engineer    Home technical assignment and review with the team    Culture fit interview and meet the team    Reference check and offer    Support: We value diversity and aim to create an inclusive experience for all applicants. Please let us know if there's anything we can do to make the process more accessible for you.  Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging  We're committed to enabling everyone to feel included and valued at work. We believe our company and culture are strongest when composed of diverse experiences and backgrounds.  That's also why we have flexible working hours, trust people to work in a hybrid environment, and extended parental leave.  All qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, family, gender identity, marital status, national origin, physical or mental disability, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. job.description: About the Role   There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.  Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. We believe products will greatly reduce hallucinations.  Our objective is to organise anyone's life, allowing us all to spend time on valuable and meaningful things.  As Product Owner, AI Email App, you work at the intersection of user needs, model capability, and engineering constraints. You will work directly with ML and engineering teams to define how the system should behave, how we measure it, and how we continuously improve it.  This is a deeply technical, hands-on role. You are expected to understand the system and challenge technical decisions.     What You'll Own     Define end-to-end requirements for AI capabilities, from model behavior to system behavior to user experience.    Translate model capabilities, evaluation results, and technical constraints into clear product and system decisions.    Make trade-offs across quality, latency, cost, reliability, safety, and UX.    Work closely with ML, backend, and client engineers on system design, evaluation, and iteration.    Define and evolve evaluation frameworks across offline metrics, online experiments, and human feedback.    Establish clear quality bars and feedback loops for AI-powered experiences.    Drive execution through clear specifications, prioritization, and strong technical judgment.    Identify failure modes and ensure AI systems behave predictably and recover gracefully.    Own product quality end-to-end, correctness, reliability, usefulness, and user trust.       What We're Looking For      Technical     Strong computer science fundamentals and system design skills.    Solid understanding of modern ML and how AI systems behave in production.    Comfortable reading technical designs, understanding architectures, and engaging deeply with engineers.    Strong intuition for model limitations, hallucinations, evaluation, and failure modes.       Product & AI     Significant experience owning complex, technical products end-to-end.    Hands-on experience with AI-powered products, particularly LLM-based systems.    Experience with model evaluation, experimentation, prompting, or AI system iteration.    Ability to turn ambiguous problems into clear requirements, measurable outcomes, and executable plans.    Strong judgment and the ability to make decisions when the right answer is not obvious.       Mindset     Highly technical, curious, and comfortable going deep.    Strong bias toward shipping, experimentation, and learning from real-world usage.    Able to challenge engineers and researcher

job.description: About Ryft      Ryft is a regulated payment facilitator and authorised payment institution building the infrastructure layer for modern commerce platforms.  We enable marketplaces, SaaS platforms and multi-party ecosystems to embed and monetise payments natively. Our technology handles onboarding, compliance, orchestration, split payments and revenue sharing, allowing our partners to focus on growth while we manage complexity.     We are now entering the next phase of scale, expanding into new verticals and building a category-defining embedded payments platform.      About the Role   We’re hiring a Risk Operations Analyst to sit within our first line fraud and risk function, reporting to the Fraud & Risk Manager. This role is the operational backbone of how Ryft manages its relationships with acquiring and banking partners, taking inbound queries from our acquires and bank partners and owning them through to resolution.  The core of this role is investigative. When a query comes in from a banking partner, we need someone who can trace a transaction end-to-end through our systems, understand what the bank is actually asking, produce a response that meets their expectations, and critically, question what they find along the way rather than closing the thread at the first plausible answer. job.description: We're a growing team of engineers, operators and technicians from diverse backgrounds, including consumer tech, finance and media, and companies like Dyson, Shopify, Meta and Tesla. It's still the early days of building the company, and this is a chance to make an outsized impact on a problem that matters. From day one, you'll be working with an experienced founding team, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural, alongside other renowned investors.  Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with a fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house, hardware and software. Our work involves building robots in our workshop and houses on real construction sites, so we're onsite five days a week.  Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about  our vision  and  company . You might enjoy our  YouTube Channel ,  Based in Europe’s film on how we’re fixing Europe’s housing shortage , or  this video by Andreas Klinger of what our office looks like .  About the role  You’ll transport robots that build houses. You’ll load them at our Amsterdam workshop, get them onto construction sites, and bring them back for repairs before their next job. When a team needs a replacement robot to keep building, you’re the person who gets it there.  We’re hiring our first Robot Transporter. We already have 150+ robots in the field and we’re expanding from the Netherlands into the UK and US. You’ll be the first person dedicated to getting our robots, equipment and materials where they need to be, helping more teams build more homes.  Your day could take you from the workshop to several active construction sites, delivering robots, collecting systems for repair and getting equipment to the next crew. You’ll work out the order of stops, what fits in each vehicle, and how to load and secure it safely. You’ll drive a C-licence box truck or B-licence van, work closely with our deployment team, and get to know the robots and the people building with them.  This is practical, physical work with room to take charge. You’ll start by planning alongside the deployment team, then take ownership of routes and transport requests as you learn the sites and loads. Plans change, sites get muddy, and teams depend on you. You’ll see the houses going up and know you helped get them built.  What you'll do     Drive.  Operate our leased C-licence box truck and our B-licence van across the Netherlands, usually two or more movements a day. When a move needs a flatbed with forklift loading, you arrange it.     Plan the day’s transport.  Work with the deployment team on the day’s plan: what goes in which vehicle, and the order of drop-offs and pick-ups across sites, our Groningen hub and our Amsterdam locations. Over time, more of this becomes yours to own.     Load and secure.  Robots, hoisting cages, scaffolding, inventory kits, equipment. You know weight limits, lashing and what it takes to get a 400+ kg system in and out of a vehicle safely.     Run deployment logistics.  Systems, kits and operational tools out to a new site before the team arrives, back to the workshop when a build wraps, and everything in between.     Keep the fleet where it's useful.  Move idle systems from one site to another that needs them, and bring systems back for repair so that a broken robot swapped today is a wall going up tomorrow.     Own the vehicles.  Servicing, inspections, cleaning, fuel, damage reporting and fines. Vehicles are always road-ready.     Log every move.  Each transport is recorded in our fleet tooling so deployment managers see when their request is planned and the company always knows where every system and kit is.     Improve the process.  Feed what you see on the road back to the inventory team (packing standards), deployment team (equipment ratios per site) and the team building our transport tooling.     Help with inventory in downtime.  When there's nothing to move, you work with the inventory team to prepare kits, organise stock and check returned equipment back in.    What we're looking for     A valid C licence with Code 95 and a driver card (bestuurderskaart) (required).      Professional driving and load securing experience (required).  Trucks, ideally box trucks with tail lift, with real responsibility for what was in the back: lashing, weight distribution, awkward loads. Equipment rental, construction logistics, removals or last-mile delivery are all good backgrounds.     Comfortable with physical work.  Loading heavy systems with the right equipment, early starts, all weather, construction site conditions. You don’t need a robotics or construction background, but you should want to know how the systems you’re moving work.     Organised in chaos.  You can hold a day with five drop-offs in your head, re-sequence it when a site calls, and still log everything at the end.     Reliable and careful.  A damaged robot costs a build day. You check straps twice and say no to an overloaded vehicle.     Clear communication.  You deal with deployment managers, site crews and the workshop every day, in person and on Slack. You raise problems early.     Based in the Netherlands.  Able to work from Amsterdam and drive to sites nationwide. We can't support relocation or visa sponsorship for this role.     English required; Dutch is a plus.     Nice to have    Forklift certificate (heftruckcertificaat)    VCA safety certificate (we can arrange it)    Basic mechanical sense: you notice when something on a vehicle or a system doesn't look right    Experience planning for more than one driver or vehicle    Comfortable with simple apps and forms for logging work    Why Monumental?  Joining Monumental means being at the forefront of a movement aimed at making significant strides in the construction industry. Here, your work has the potential to impact not just the company but the future of how we build. If you're driven by innovation, eager to tackle complex challenges, and ready to make a tangible difference, we want to hear from you.  For open applications (where you don't see an exact role match), please reach out to us at:   Unfortunately we do not currently support internships.  If you don't meet all the qualifications here but are excited about Monumental and feel you'd still be able to help us tackle complex challenges, do get in touch. We welcome generalists who focus on outcomes and are eager to learn on the job.  Find more  English Speaking Jobs in Netherlands  on Arbeitnow

job.description:
Build the next generation of autonomous construction robotics  
 At MESH, we develop autonomous robotic systems that automate end-to-end rebar construction. Bridging digital design and physical automation, our multidisciplinary team transforms advanced robotics research into robust, production-ready industrial systems deployed globally. 
 Tasks 
  Role description  
 We are looking for a Robotics Software Engineer to develop and productize software across the full robotics stack from perception and motion planning to control and system integration. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who enjoys working across subsystem boundaries. You will take ownership of the engineering work required to turn promising research and algorithms into robust and mature capabilities that can be deployed and maintained in real-world robotic systems. 
 What You Will Work On 
 You will contribute across the full robotics software stack, including: 
 
 Perception: 2D/3D sensing, point-cloud processing, object and feature detection, pose estimation, calibration. 
 Motion Planning: collision checking, trajectory generation and optimization, kinematics, robot/world modeling, and integration of planning algorithms. 
 Robot Control: integration with industrial robot controllers, HAL layers, trajectory execution, real-time or near-real-time control interfaces, state monitoring, and coordination of multi-robotic systems. 
 System Integration: connecting robotics SW, application logic, hardware, and external systems into reliable end-to-end robotic applications. 
 Robotics Infrastructure: reusable software components, interfaces, configuration, logging, diagnostics, testing, simulation, and deployment infrastructure. 
 
 Your Responsibilities 
 
 Design, implement, test, and maintain robotics software primarily in C++ and Python. 
 Develop and integrate components across the full robotics SW stack. 
 Take algorithms and prototypes and mature them into reliable software components. 
 Build automated tests, simulation-based tests, hardware-in-the-loop tests, and system-level validation where appropriate. 
 Work with industrial robots, sensors, cameras, external axes, and other automation hardware. 
 Develop clean interfaces between robotics algorithms, hardware drivers, application software, and higher-level systems. 
 Diagnose complex problems that span software, algorithms, networking, robot controllers, sensors, and hardware. 
 Improve observability through structured logging, diagnostics, error reporting, and system health monitoring. 
 Support deployment, commissioning, troubleshooting, and validation of robotic systems. 
 
 Requirements 
  What We Are Looking For  
 Required 
 
 Masters degree or higher in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or a related field. 
 Strong software engineering skills in C++, with working knowledge of Python. 
 Experience developing software for robotic or other complex hardware systems. 
 Good understanding of several areas of robotics, such as, motion and trajectory planning, robot control, vision, sensor and robot calibration. 
 Experience with robotics middleware such as ROS/ROS2 or similar 
 Comfortable working with Linux and modern software development workflows using Git, code reviews, build systems, debugging tools, and automated testing. 
 Ability to debug problems across multiple layers of a robotic system rather than treating individual components in isolation. 
 Strong understanding of software architecture, modularity, interfaces, and maintainability. 
 
 Experience in one or more of the following would be an advantage: 
 
 3D perception using point clouds, depth cameras, stereo systems. 
 Libraries such as Eigen, PCL, OpenCV, or similar. 
 Collision detection, robot/world modeling, trajectory optimization, or numerical optimization. 
 Real-time or high-performance robot communication and control. 
 Profiling, performance optimization, concurrency, and multithreaded C++. 
 Deploying and supporting robotic systems outside a controlled R&D environment. 
 CI/CD and automated testing for robotics software. 
 Experience working with industrial robotic arms such as ABB 
 
 We do not expect you to be an expert in every part of the robotics stack. We are looking for strong software engineering fundamentals, depth in one or more robotics areas, and the ability and interest to work across subsystem boundaries. 
  Eligibility  
 Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Switzerland or be eligible to obtain the required Swiss work authorization without employer-sponsored visa support. 
  Why Join MESH?  
 At MESH, you will work on robotics problems where advanced R&D meets real-world industrial deployment. Our goal is not only to develop new robotics capabilities, but to turn them into systems that solve challenging problems in real world deployments. 
 
 You will have opportunities to work across the full robotics SW stack including system integration, and the software architecture connecting them rather than being restricted to a narrow subsystem. 
 You will work directly on the engineering challenges that take robotics from promising prototypes to robust, repeatable, and deployable solutions. 
 Solve challenging real-world robotics problems. Work with industrial robots, 3D vision systems, complex environments, and applications where conventional automation approaches reach their limits. 
 See your work operate on real hardware. Develop software that moves beyond simulation and demos and becomes part of robotic systems deployed in real production environments. 
 Have impact across the system. As part of a small, multidisciplinary engineering team, you will work closely across robotics, software, and hardware, with the opportunity to influence both technical decisions and how our robotics platform evolves.

While nature took billions of years to perfect molecules, we are harnessing AI to unlock trillion-dollar materials breakthroughs in months, not millennia. Our founding team is the most cited in the world, comprised of world-class researchers in AI, chemistry and engineering.  We are working on some of the hardest and most important challenges including energy, clean water, the future of compute, and carbon capture, and this is just the start of what our 'search engine' for next-generation materials will unlock. The Role   Due to rapid growth in our partner lab network, we are seeking a Scientific Product Manager to join our Product team and bring partner labs and their experimental workflows onto the CuspAI platform.     Your impact   This is an exciting opportunity to join the product team at CuspAI, working closely with materials scientists, ML researchers and platform engineers to make AI-driven experimentation work in real laboratories. As one of a small team of Scientific Product Managers, you will take ownership of a set of partner labs and the lab integration work around them, translating what each lab actually needs into requirements our engineers and ML researchers can build against. Alongside the product work, you will spend real time with your partners' teams and their experimental data. job.description: Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.    We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.    Here’s what this particular role covers.      🛠️ About our Map & Route Team   Our Map & Route team sits within Wayve’s Automotive Platforms division in Vehicle Software Engineering, and builds the geospatial foundations behind our AI driver. Working with global-scale data, the team turns road-network and navigation data into reliable products used across Wayve, building geospatial services and data products to support company operations. We work with our model development, experimentation, and evaluation platforms to build an AI driver that uses maps and navigation data like an expert human driver by using map information to enhance training and evaluation of performance. We are a full-stack team owning mapping end to end, getting to touch work that is infrastructure, data engineering, data science, backend and frontend.      🧠 Your day-to-day     Write full-stack services in Python and Typescript, creating novel geospatial services to solve challenging and unique problems we face in building our AI driving products.    Collaborate with internal teams to understand requirements and build solutions with global geospatial data.    Design and build data pipelines with PySpark and Databricks to enrich fleet data with mapping and road-network information at global scale.    Build applications and datasets that support route planning and the preparation of map data for training and simulation.    Integrate with navigation and mapping APIs from providers such as Mapbox, TomTom and Google Maps.    Maintain, support and improve the services the team already runs.    Deploy and operate your services on Azure and Kubernetes, owning them end to end.        🧩 What you’ll be working on     Global-scale geospatial enrichment pipelines that tell us where we’ve driven and what the road network looks like.    Route-planning applications and datasets that help our teams decide where to drive next.    Map data preparation for model training and simulation.    New services you’ll take from idea to production and lead end to end.        🙌 You should apply if     You are a strong, hands-on Python engineer who can deliver high-quality production code at pace.    You are comfortable with an AI-assisted or AI engineering workflow (ideation, planning, implementation and review).    You have built and operated large-scale data pipelines using Spark or PySpark.    You are comfortable writing SQL to query and analyse large datasets.    You have working knowledge of cloud infrastructure and container orchestration, ideally Azure and Kubernetes, and are happy to own deployment, monitoring, and observability of your services.    You enjoy taking ownership of new services and seeing them through end to end.    Experience with geospatial data processing, road-network data or routing engines (e.g. OpenStreetMap, TomTom, HERE or Overture data, PostGIS, navigation APIs) would be a strong advantage.    Experience with Bazel or monorepo build systems is desirable but not mandatory.    Experience with workflow orchestration tools such as Flyte or Airflow would be a bonus.       🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.      More about Wayve:   🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.  Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.      How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:   Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.      🔍 The Interview Process:   Our process is clear and respectful of your time:     Initial call / recruiter screen  (30 mins)     Competency interviews : Python Programming (60 mins) and Hiring Manager interview (45 mins)     Deep-dive technical interviews : Systems Design (60 mins) and Domain interview (60 mins)     Final interview : Mission and Values Alignment (45 mins).    We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.      What’s in it for you (Location dependant):   💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually 📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve ✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable ✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs 📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth 🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more  A quick, honest note before you apply.  Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.    If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.  At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.   For more information visit  Careers at Wayve.  To learn more about what drives us, visit  Values at Wayve   DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory. At JetBrains, code is our passion. Ever since we started, back in 2000, we have strived to make the strongest, most effective developer tools on earth. By automating routine checks and corrections, our tools speed up production, freeing developers to grow, discover, and create.

We just unveiled JetBrains Central,  a platform for agent-driven software development that connects tools, agents, and infrastructure. It enables automated AI workflows to run, be monitored, and be managed across teams – with clear visibility into results, costs, and performance.

JetBrains Central provides three core capabilities:
Governance and control: Policy enforcement, identity and access management, observability, auditability, and cost attribution for agent-driven work. Some of these functionalities are already available via the JetBrains Central Console.
Agent execution infrastructure: Cloud agent runtimes and computation provisioning that allow agents to run reliably across development environments.
Agent optimization and context: Shared semantic context across repositories and projects, enabling agents to access relevant knowledge, and task routing to the most appropriate models or tools.

Inside the Professional Services department, we are building a team of Forward Deployed Engineers to help our customers adopt AI-native development with JetBrains Central and enable JetBrains consulting partners to transform their customers’ AI-native software development lifecycle.

About the role

As a Principal Forward Deployed Engineer, you will work directly with early adopter customers to deploy JetBrains Central platform into complex enterprise environments and help them move from experimental AI usage to governed, scalable AI-native development.

You will act as a trusted advisor to customer engineering teams and consulting partners, while also mentoring other Forward Deployed Engineers and helping with complex deployments. In this role, you will help establish best practices for enterprise AI adoption and influence how organizations implement AI-driven software development.

This role is often a strong fit for engineers who have previously served as Principal or Staff Engineers, Heads of Engineering, CTOs, or Solutions Architects and who enjoy working directly with customers while staying deeply involved with complex technical systems.

This role combines consulting, architecture, and hands-on engineering. Your work in the field will directly influence how our platform evolves and how enterprises adopt AI-driven development.

You will work directly with the world’s most innovative companies — our client base includes 420 of the Fortune 500 — ensuring they maximize the value of their JetBrains investments.

What you’ll do

job.description:
About us  
   
 Aave Labs began with a simple question: how do we make financial services like borrowing, saving, and earning more accessible globally? 
   
 We built the Aave Protocol, now the world’s largest and most trusted onchain lending market, connecting decentralized finance with individuals, traditional finance, and fintech. 
   
 Today, we build trusted, high-quality products that expand access to lending, credit, and savings globally 
   
  Our culture  
   
 We build trusted products that help people access and discover economic opportunities. 
   
 We hold a high bar for quality and craftsmanship. No detail is too small. Trust depends on it. 
   
 We’re a global team building products people can actually use, turning complex technology into something simple and reliable. 
   
 We stay aligned, move quickly, and think long term, while keeping teams lean and focused on impact. 
   
  About the Role  
 
 
 
 We're looking for a Staff Frontend Engineer who operates across the full picture - someone who deeply understands how great web interfaces are built and how they perform, works autonomously, and translates that knowledge into exceptional web products and design systems. 
 Financial products are complex. Our users range from first-timers to power users, and the challenge of making that experience clear, fast, and trustworthy is one we take seriously. At this level, you're not just executing - you're bringing product intuition to the work, identifying where things break down, and making calls that shape the direction of what we build. 
   How you can make an impact:  
 Work autonomously across our web products, building high-quality UI with a strong point of view on how it should feel, function, and perform 
 Own and evolve complex, reusable components within the Aave design system - setting the standard for quality and consistency 
 Set the bar for frontend performance, from data loading, fetching and caching patterns through to server rendering and streaming 
 Bring product-level thinking to everything you work on - understanding user needs, business context, and technical constraints, whilst balancing them well 
 Collaborate with our talented designers, engineers, and product leads to bring clarity to ambiguous problems 
 Help raise the bar for the team through the quality of your work and the way you approach problems 
  Let's connect if you have:  
 Strong proficiency in React, TypeScript, CSS and system design and architecture 
 Deep experience with frontend performance engineering - measuring it, diagnosing it, and fixing it 
 Strong command of Next.js patterns for data loading, fetching and caching, and experience handling server rendering and streaming data to the frontend 
 Deep experience with component-driven design systems and component design patterns, and building for consistency at scale 
 The product sense to work without a detailed brief - you can identify what needs to be solved, not just how to solve it

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.  We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.    The role in one line  As our first EMEA Strategic Customer Success Manager, you’ll help define what strategic success looks like at  incident.io , and become the trusted partner who makes us core to how the biggest enterprises run reliability.  What that looks like day to day  You’ll work with a small number of our largest, most complex and highest-value customers. These are established, often global and regulated enterprises, where buying decisions take time, many business units are involved, and incident management is part of a wider move away from legacy tools and processes. You’ll be their strategic partner across the full lifecycle, from early involvement in the deal with Sales through to adoption and expansion, and from the on-call engineer to the CIO and CTO.  You’ll help land strategic logos with focused first contracts, then build the business case and success plan that turns them into larger deals. From there you’ll expand across the enterprise, mapping the organisation, finding champions and repeating proven wins across business units and regions. You’ll run Executive Business Reviews and connect our leadership with theirs, tying what we do to what matters to their business: operational resilience, regulatory risk, the cost of downtime, tool consolidation, MTTR reduction and incident process maturity.  You’ll lead onboarding and migrations in organisations that move carefully, moving them off legacy tools and ITSM-led processes and making the change stick, including deeper adoption across Response, On-call, Status Pages and our AI capabilities. You’ll spot and reduce business, operational and reputational risk before it becomes visible, and bring Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Marketing and Support together around shared goals for each account, including expansion and renewals.  You’ll also work directly with Product and Engineering on the roadmap and design partnerships. As the first EMEA Strategic CSM and third on the team overall, you’ll help define our strategic CS playbook, support high-stakes deals and help develop your peers as the segment grows. job.description:
The Opportunity  
  The infrastructure that runs the modern world (power grids, data centres, fibre networks, EV charging) is being built out faster than at any point in a generation. The companies doing that work are drowning in the volume, variety, and velocity of it. Sitetracker is how they stay ahead of it.  
   
  Sitetracker is the AI-native platform for infrastructure lifecycle management, covering project, construction, operations, and asset management in one system of record. Scout, our enterprise AI agent platform, is what sets us apart. Scout does the work, not just reports on it, and it stays grounded in the customer's own data so the answers are trustworthy enough to act on. That is what holds up in an enterprise procurement review when a bolted-on chatbot does not.  
   
  You will be our go-to Strategic Account Executive for the Middle East territory. Your job is to grow revenue and to shape how Sitetracker leads the AI-native transformation of digital infrastructure across the Middle East. You will own a priority territory with strong product-market fit, backed by proven customer outcomes, a differentiated platform, and strong demand generation.  
   
  Our top performers work as enterprise advisors. They bring strategic thinking, curiosity, and real customer empathy. They own outcomes, not quotas. If you raise the bar, love winning new logos, and want autonomy, scale, and purpose, this is a role worth a serious look.  
   
  What You'll Do  
  You will join a sales team that pairs start-up pace with enterprise ambition. This is a build role, not an inherited book of business. You will define and execute the go-to-market strategy for your territory, engage new prospects, and guide them through high-stakes decisions with precision and insight.  
   
  Every deal moves the industry forward, whether that is energising a new grid interconnection, standing up a data centre, upgrading a telecom network, or scaling EV charging. You will orchestrate complex buying journeys across large stakeholder groups, partner cross-functionally with product, marketing, and services, and earn the trust of executives on both sides. This is a quota-carrying role in a MEDDPICC environment, and it is also a chance to lead, to sell a genuinely differentiated platform, and to leave a mark.  
   
  You will be selling into a market that is actively rethinking how it uses AI. Part of the job is separating signal from hype: showing skeptical enterprise buyers what agentic AI grounded in their own operational data actually changes about how their teams work, and what it is worth.  
   
  The Skills You'll Have  
  Enterprise Sales  
 
  Demonstrates evidence of selling in the Middle Eastern markets  
  Strong evidence of success selling complex SaaS solutions across mid-market, large, and enterprise accounts, ideally in Telecom, Energy, or adjacent infrastructure sectors.  
  Can walk through, in detail, how you navigate a complex enterprise SaaS deal to a win

job.description: Role:  VLA Pre-training Engineer / Deep Learning Engineer – World Models (2 openings)  Company:   Humanoid   Location:  London, UK (King’s Cross) – on-site, five days a week  Job Type:  Full-time   About Humanoid   Humanoid is building the world’s most capable, commercially scalable and safe humanoid robots. Its platform, HMND-01, is already deployed in real industrial environments, which makes Humanoid the most serious humanoid robotics company in Europe.    300+ people, 34+ nationalities, flat structure: your decisions ship directly into real robots.    Offices in London (HQ, King’s Cross), Boston, Vancouver and San Diego.    Values: Speed, Ambition, Passion, Trust.     About the role   The VLA Core team builds the base vision-language-action model that the entire manipulation pipeline depends on. This is deep learning at scale: training models from scratch on multi-embodiment trajectory corpora and internet-scale video, with real deployment constraints. The model has to fit and run on a real robot.  Robotics experience is not required. If you come from LLMs, VLMs or video generation, be ready to get up to speed on a new domain quickly.  This is a senior individual contributor role with no management track. The team is research-adjacent, but the output is models that run on robots. Results are shared as blog posts, not papers.  There are two tracks in one team. They are the same role with a different focus, so you can lean into either.   Track 1: VLA Pre-training     Pre-train base models on a diverse multi-embodiment corpus of trajectories, fine-tune policies to excel at specific tasks and explore synthetic data.    Post-train policies with behaviour cloning and RL, and own the full loop from data to deployment.    Partner with the Data Collection team: specify what good data looks like, identify failure modes, ensure diversity and coverage.    Run pre-, mid- and post-training on the VLA stack; explore new modalities and architecture changes.    Build and maintain continuous pipelines: ingest synthetic data and teleop logs, version them, apply weak-supervision labelling, curate balanced datasets and automatically surface fresh failure cases into retraining.    Work with the MLOps and Data Platform teams to scale distributed training and optimize models for real-time edge inference on the robot.     Track 2: World Models     Design and train multimodal, action-conditioned world models (video, state, action and language) using diffusion-based and transformer architectures.    Build video prediction and dynamics models that stay physically consistent over long horizons, including contact-rich manipulation, and serve as pretrained priors for VLA policies.    Develop learned-simulator evaluation: score candidate policies offline, predict real-world success rates before deployment, roll out policy futures for safety review and planning.    Generate synthetic rollouts and counterfactual experience (rare events, cross-platform and sim-to-real transfer) and measure their effect on downstream task performance.    Build data pipelines that turn fleet telemetry, teleoperation logs and internet-scale video into training corpora.    Run scaling and ablation studies on architecture, data mixture and context length.     What you need to succeed     3+ years building deep learning systems in industry or research, with shipped models or published work to show for it.    Deep hands-on experience with at least one of: LLMs, VLMs, image or video generative models (architecture, training and inference). For the World Models track: diffusion models, autoregressive transformers, latent-variable models or video prediction.    You have actually trained models yourself: pre-training runs, distributed infrastructure, the works. Connecting APIs, building agents or a quick fine-tune is not enough.    Experience with deep learning infrastructure: streaming datasets, checkpointing and state management, distributed training strategies, debugging numerics and training instabilities.    Strong Python and PyTorch or JAX. You can profile, optimize data loaders and write maintainable research code.    Strong coding fundamentals. The process includes a LeetCode-style coding round, so come prepared.    Empirical rigor: careful evaluations, honest baselines, clear experiment docs, crisp communication of trade-offs.    You are proactive: you can take an open, messy problem and drive it without waiting for a spec.    Working English.     Nice to have     Robotics or autonomous driving experience; familiarity with simulators (Isaac Sim, MuJoCo) and sim-to-real.    Experience applying RL to LLMs or robotics.    Experience with VLA models; familiarity with OpenVLA, Physical Intelligence (π) models or similar open-source frameworks.    Experience with world models for robotics or autonomous driving (action-conditioned video models, learned simulators, model-based RL).    Proven productization of deep nets: latency and throughput constraints, on-device optimization, fast inference for generative models.    Publications at top-tier DL conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CoRL, CVPR) or equivalent open-source contributions.     Interview process     Intro call with Igor, hirehire’s AI researcher.    HR screen with Humanoid.    Coding round (LeetCode-style).    Specialization interview (pre-training or world models).    Technical execution interview: how you work, collaborate and drive problems.    Optional chat with a tech leader.     What you get     Salary: a wide range, set by the level you show in the interviews.    Equity: stock options with meaningful upside as Humanoid scales.    30+ paid days off: 23 days annual leave, all UK bank holidays and a company shutdown between Christmas and New Year.    Private healthcare: fully funded, including virtual and in-person care.    Pension: 8% total contribution (5% employee, 3% employer) on full earnings.    Daily food: free breakfast, catered lunch and snacks in the office.    Real ownership: direct access to founding leadership, real input on product direction and room to drive key initiatives from day one.    Visa sponsorship and relocation to London. job.description: Position Description The Operations Systems Support (OSS) team within ESB Networks' Distribution Markets and System Operations (DMSO) function are seeking to fill the role of Senior IT/Operational Technology (OT) Systems and Integration Engineer. The role of the OSS team is to support and maintain ESB Networks mission critical OT systems enable the monitoring, control, and management of Ireland's electricity distribution network. These include Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA), Electricity Distribution Network Management System (NMS) and Geographic Information System (GIS). These systems support real-time network operations, outage management, fault response, service restoration, and data exchange across multiple business and operational platforms. This role provides a unique opportunity to support capabilities that form part of Ireland's critical national infrastructure. You will work at the forefront of Operational Technology, supporting the processes that underpin transformation of the electricity network as ESB Networks delivers the systems required for increased renewable generation, network flexibility, electrification and the transition to a net-zero future The Senior IT/OT Systems and Integration Engineer is responsible for supporting, maintaining and enhancing ESB Networks’ critical Operational Technology systems, including NMS, SCADA and associated applications. The role ensures these business-critical platforms remain secure, resilient and available to support network operations, outage management and service restoration. Working closely with business and technology stakeholders, you will help deliver the technologies that support the ongoing transformation of Ireland’s electricity network. The position involves delivering enhancements to the existing OT systems, supporting system upgrades and patch deployments, troubleshooting complex technical issues, and carrying out data management activities such as housekeeping, environment refreshes, and data integrity maintenance. The Senior IT/OT Systems & Integration Engineer is also responsible for developing and maintaining custom interfaces and integrations between OT systems and ESB or third-party applications ensuring seamless data exchange and operational effectiveness across the organisation. A key element of the role is working with OT vendors, providing oversight across system support and enhancement activities. Responsibilities include reviewing and approving change requests, supporting the implementation of new functionality, coordinating problem resolution, and engaging with vendor support teams at all levels to ensure timely and effective issue management. In addition to technical responsibilities, the role has a strong focus on knowledge management and capability development. This includes producing and maintaining high-quality technical documentation, standard operating procedures, configuration records, user guides, and operational runbooks to support effective system operation and support. The Senior IT/OT Systems & Integration Engineer will also play an important role in mentoring and developing junior team members, promoting knowledge transfer, supporting structured training programmes, and building sustainable technical capability within the Technical Operations team. Key Responsibilities: Support and maintain ESB Networks critical OT systems, including Electricity Distribution NMS and SCADA, ensuring the system availability, reliability, and performance. Support, maintain, and enhance custom Electricity Distribution NMS reporting functionality to meet operational and business reporting requirements. Perform data maintenance activities, including data maintenance and data quality activities, validation, and data refreshes across OT environments. Support the development and optimisation of advanced Distribution Management System (DMS) capabilities including, Power Flow Analysis, Fault Location, Isolation and Service Restoration (FLISR), Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems (DERMS), Load Forecasting, Network Optimisation. Delivery of enhancement projects for the existing OT systems, ensuring alignment with operational and strategic objectives. Support testing activities, including system, integration, user acceptance, and regression testing for upgrades, enhancements, and new functionality. Work closely with the wider OSS team, OT Delivery, Enterprise IT Services, the OT vendors, and business stakeholders to ensure the successful operation and continuous improvement of critical real-time operational systems. Work closely with other areas of the business to understand operational requirements, address system issues, and deliver effective technology solutions. Maintain regular engagement and communication with team members, business stakeholders, vendors, and support teams to ensure effective service delivery and project execution. Support knowledge management and capability development including producing and maintaining high-quality technical documentation, standard operating procedures, configuration records, user guides, and operational runbooks to support effective system operation and support Supervise, mentor, and support junior team members, promoting collaboration, knowledge sharing, and technical skill development. Experience supporting testing activities, including System Testing, Integration Testing, User Acceptance Testing, and Regression Testing. Ability to produce and maintain high-quality technical documentation, operational procedures, and support documentation. Self-motivated with the ability to manage personal workload while supporting wider team objectives. job.description: About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and open up new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a lot of work ahead. That gives you an unusual opportunity to help put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team The Startup SaaS Platforms team works with European startups in one of Stripe’s must-win segments. SaaS platforms are companies that use Stripe to embed payments and make financial services a core part of their products, such as Shopify, Mindbody, and Lightspeed. For these companies, their partnership with Stripe is vital to the success of their businesses. SaaS platforms are a global priority for Stripe, and our team finds and wins Stripe’s future strategic accounts in Europe. We partner with high-potential companies early and help them use Stripe’s solutions to better support their users, scale globally, and create new revenue streams by monetising payments and financial services. What you’ll do We’re hiring an Account Executive to win new business with pre-revenue and early-stage SaaS platform startups across the United Kingdom and Ireland. This is a new-logo role. Your job is to find the most promising founders building platforms today, win their business for Stripe before they choose another provider, and get them live with the right integration from day one. You’ll work alongside our SaaS Platform Account Executives as the team’s dedicated hunter for the earliest stage of the market. You’ll own the pre-revenue and early-revenue segment end to end, from generating pipeline and handling inbound demand to closing deals and getting each new platform activated. Early-stage platforms make their payments decisions early and rarely revisit them. They also often need several products from the start, including embedded payments, connected-account onboarding, payouts, and monetisation. Winning them early and selling the right solution gives Stripe a lasting position with the platforms that will scale fastest. This is a high-velocity sales role with short cycles, a high volume of opportunities, and plenty of competitive deals. Responsibilities Build and run your own pipeline. Prospect high-potential pre-revenue and early-stage SaaS platforms across the United Kingdom and Ireland, and turn inbound interest from early-stage platforms into qualified opportunities. Win new logos. Run fast, consultative sales cycles from discovery to close and win competitive evaluations against other payments providers. Sell the right solution from the start. Understand each founder’s business model and position the right Stripe Connect integration and payments monetisation strategy so that new platforms are set up to scale. Close and activate. Negotiate and close deals, then work with Solutions Architects, Product, Risk, and Operations to get new platforms live quickly. You’ll be measured on new business won and activated. Source new business through the ecosystem. Build relationships with founders, venture capital firms, accelerators, and startup communities across the United Kingdom and Ireland to create pipeline and grow Stripe’s presence among early-stage founders. Work with the SaaS Platform Account Executive team. Share market intelligence on emerging platforms and pass on accounts that have moved beyond the early stage so that each seller can focus on the opportunities where they can have the greatest impact. Bring what you learn from the market back to Product and go-to-market teams to sharpen how Stripe wins early-stage platforms. Who you are You’re a self-starting hunter who enjoys finding and winning new business. job.description: Overview Susquehanna is looking for highly motivated full-time students for our 10-week quantitative strategy development summer internship program based at our EU Headquarters in Dublin, Ireland. This is a computationally intensive role that will allow you to use your strong technical skills to solve problems at the intersection of trading, quant and technology. Throughout the summer, you will receive education about how markets work by going through a deep dive into financial markets and Susquehanna's approach to trading. You will also work on challenging projects for our trading strategy development teams in spaces such as signal creation and detection, quantitative strategy analysis, and low latency C++ strategy development. Additionally, you'll have the opportunity to work on projects side by side with senior developers who understand the nuances of building complex tr ading strategies. Our quantitative strategy developers are part of our high-performing team s that build some of the most powerful trading systems in the finance industry. This is a computationally intensive role that will allow you to utilize both your data analysis and technology skills. What we're looking for Class of 202 8 : You are a master’s or bachelor’s student in their penultimate year of study, majoring in a quantitative and/or STEM discipline such as computer science, computer engineering, mathematics or data science for example. You intend to graduate and begin full time employment by August 2028. Clear Communicator: You enjoy building relationships with those you work closely with and are comfortable sharing ideas, expressing your thoughts, and listening to the views of others . Ambitious: You’re someone that enjoys setting personal goals and giving your all to achieve them. Be it in Arts, Sports, Academics, or another passion; you’re not afraid to put in the effort to reach your full potential. Technically Proficient: Strong software development skills in (Python and a compiled language). Experience and comfort working with data using libraries such as Pandas, Polars, or NumPy. You will have exceptional quantitative, logical reasoning, and analytical skills. Problem Solver: When it comes to solving problems, you use clear and sound reasoning. You’re rational and like to use numbers and data to come up with sensible solutions. What's in it for you: Education: We are renowned for our market-leading education and training programmes . You will attend classes covering a vast range of topics (Options Pricing, Machine Learning, Data Analysis Techniques, Game Theory, Trader Talks, In-house trading games… the list goes on!) from some of the most experienced employees in Susquehanna . Collaboration : You will get to work with a wide range of people in the classroom and through your project work; people who share a passion for mathematics, problem-solving, game theory, and technology. Culture : O ur non-hierarchical, casual, and collaborative culture allows employees of every level to thrive, and we focus on continuous development, no matter how long you’ve been in Susquehanna. Perks : We offer a highly competitive compensation package to our interns . Located in Ireland's Financial Services Centre, in the heart of Dublin's city centre , our office features free onsite catering, a games room, and a fully equipped in-house gym. Throughout the summer, interns enjoy weekly social events. For those joining us from outside Dublin, we also provide accommodation for the duration of the internship. About Susquehanna Susquehanna is a global quantitative trading firm powered by scientific rigor, curiosity, and innovation. Our culture is intellectually driven and highly collaborative, bringing together researchers, engineers, and traders to design and deploy impactful strategies in our systematic trading environment. To meet the unique challenges of global markets, Susquehanna applies machine learning and advanced quantitative research to vast datasets in order to uncover actionable insights and build effective strategies. By uniting deep market expertise with cutting-edge technology, we excel in solving complex problems and pushing boundaries together. Additional details ** We hire for our QSD internship on a rolling basis. There are limited places on our 2027 QSD internship, therefore interested candidates are strongly encouraged to apply early.* * The interview process for this role will be a series of interviews including coding, mathematics, system design and behavioural interviews. Our summer internship is 10 weeks and runs from late June to late August. Applicants for our summer internship must legally eligible to work in Ireland. Susquehanna is an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to diversity and inclusion throughout our recruitment process. If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application or recruitment process, please contact us. If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to recruiting@sig.com . Any resume or referral submitted in the absence of a signed agreement will not be eligible for an agency fee.
